release.name: v0.6.3: Oxford DIQKD re-analysis (Study 36), anytime certificate on randomised test-or-keep data
release.body: Adds the pre-registered re-analysis of the Oxford device-independent QKD characterisation run (Nadlinger et al., Nature 2022; data provided by the authors, not redistributed). Anytime certificate on kept pairs: F >= 0.917 (trusted settings), above 0.9 after 219,185 kept pairs; device-independent bound 0.837. Link over-dispersed by 1.6% without persistence. Scoreboard: 89 primary (78 pass, 11 fail).

release.name: v0.6.1 — Study 34: provable closed loop on larger grids
release.body:
Adds Study 34 to the v0.6.0 release (manuscript v0.6). No other code changed.

## New
- **Study 34 – closed loop on other grids** (`study34_grids/`): the provable closed loop (Theorem 2, current-look bound) and the always-on margin (Corollary 3) on 5×5, 10×10 (180 links) and 30×30 (1,740 links) grids, under three load settings (same total rate, matched exposure, three times the rate). Pre-registered (commit 1f5636c) before the first job; 4,928 runs.
  - 3/3 primary, 6/6 secondary PASS.
  - 0 of 4.2 M post-alarm pairs bad on 10×10 and 30×30; always-on margin 0 of 7.8 M.
  - Detection depends on the test volume, not the grid size (alarm rate 0.94 on both 5×5 and 30×30; about twice as early with three times the rate). Harm before the first alarm still dominates on every grid.
- Manuscript v0.6 updated with the Study 34 results; evidence ledger extended to E149; scoreboard: 83 primary hypotheses, 74 PASS, 9 FAIL.

release.name: v0.6.0 — Provable closed loop, IBM hardware runs, robustness (manuscript v0.6)
release.body:
Code, pre-registrations, run outputs and audit trail for manuscript v0.6 of
"Certifying delivered entanglement: per-pair guarantees need a model, averages do not".

## New since v0.5.0
- **Study 30 – provable closed loop** (`study30_closed_loop/`): after a model-check alarm, the margin is a time-uniform upper confidence bound on the model offset (Theorem 2); run from the start it protects every user (Corollary 3). Offset placed in the true state. 5/5 primary, 6/6 secondary PASS. Detection is the bottleneck: most harm occurs before the first alarm.
- **Studies 31 and 31b – IBM hardware** (`study31_hardware_testkeep/`, `study31b_hardware_detector/`): test-or-keep on ibm_fez with Bell-basis ground truth. Certificate valid in both runs. Study 31: fixed-bet check missed the injected degradation (W3 FAIL, disclosed). Study 31b: hybrid check alarmed (W1–W3, W5 PASS).
- **Study 32 – recovering bound and robustness** (`study32_robustness/`): the offset bound need not be a running minimum; it recovered in 128/128 forced-miscoverage runs at no cost. Guarantees hold at τ = 0.85/0.92 and with less calibration data. 6/6 primary, 5/5 secondary PASS.
- **S33 – fixed-K vs anytime certificate** (`study33_fixedk/`, computation, not pre-registered).
- **Disclosure:** Studies 28–29 added the offset to the model, which inflated detection power (ledger E134).
- Evidence ledger extended to E145; scoreboard: 80 primary hypotheses, 71 PASS, 9 FAIL.

Every confirmatory study was pre-registered and pushed before its first job; failures are reported.
Third-party datasets are not redistributed (see `DATA_SOURCES.md`).

release.name: v0.5.0: Margin response (Study 29): closed-loop model check with tracking margin
release.body:
Study 29 (pre-registered; commit a779735 before the first job): after a model-check alarm, the margin tracks an exact upper bound on the model offset (post-alarm and probe tests) and can come back down.
- 0 bad pairs in 5.8M post-alarm deliveries; Study 28's failure case fixed (0/128 vs 127/128).
- Margin within +0.006-0.011 of the true offset; throughput 0.78 of oracle vs 0.48 (Study 28) and 0.35-0.53 (16-point tomography).
6/6 primary, 4/4 secondary PASS. PSC and cloud analyses identical. Ledger E123-E125.

release.name: v0.4.0: Model-checked delivery (Study 28), converse resource bound, network-wide guarantee
release.body:
Study 28 (pre-registered; commit 023faed before the first job): the certification tests also check the per-pair guard's model.
- Detected undeclared model error in 128/128 ion networks; 70-92% fewer bad pairs; false alarms 0.29%.
- H4 FAILED (disclosed): one network's early alarm raised the margin too little; 0.8% bad after alarms (bar 1%).
- Blind to sparse failures and thin hardware, as predicted.
- Network-wide guarantee: 0/128 networks with a bad pair, cost 0.5 points on ions.
- Converse bound: certifying 0.9 needs >= 330 kept pairs (p = 0.1); our certificate needs 678.
6/7 primary, 4/4 secondary PASS. PSC and cloud analyses identical. Ledger E120-E122.

release.name: v0.2.0 — Study 25 results: realism checks (model error, calibration, shared noise, network load, drift)
release.body:
Confirmatory results for Study 25, pre-registered in v0.1.4 (DOI 10.5281/zenodo.23289143).

- 9/9 primary hypotheses PASS; 2/3 secondary PASS.
- Secondary T3 FAILS (disclosed, not re-tuned): under strong shared noise, the time-split AI variant on NV exceeded the known-law guard by 2.12 points of bad paths vs a 2.00 margin. The main AI arm passed on all hardware.
- Run outputs: des_s25_psc/runs.csv (sha256 3826490a…), des_s25d_psc/runs.csv (7bb3996c…); analysis re-run independently with identical results.
- Timing: hash-locked on the cluster before job submission; publicly pushed before any job produced output (ledger E102).

See study25_realism/RESULTS_25.md and audit/EVIDENCE_LEDGER.md (E101–E103).
